messages:
Maya Thompson: follow-up from the long-term refactor board: proposal to surgically split session-mesh into two bounded services: session-router (hotpath, short-lived routing decisions) and session-archive (durable state + long tail ops). goal: reduce hot hotpath contention, make archive paydown and compaction independent, and shrink runtime surface for latency-sensitive calls. thinking incremental canary by tenant cohort. high-level plan below. feedback?

Evan Li: +1. We need to be explicit about read/write ownership during coexistence. do we plan dual-write for a period or shadow-write?

Maya Thompson: plan is dual-write for writes, read-from-router first (fast cache), fallback to archive. Archive exposes a compact lookup API optimized for large scans and compaction workers. Router keeps small in-memory routing state and a local LRU cache for last-touch tenants.

Rafael Ortiz: curious about compaction/paydown work. if archive runs compaction that renames keys or re-assigns shards we need routing invalidation. how do we propagate? event bus or versioned pointers?

Maya Thompson: prefer versioned pointers. router cache entries include pointer_version and last_seen_ts. archive will emit pointer_version bumps when it moves data. router invalidates on consumer events or TTL. keeps things simple: eventual consistency with short TTL.

Priya Nair: concern: generation path calls into router synchronously. extra hop may add jitter. can we co-locate router with hot serving plane? or embed a tiny local cache that is authoritative for p99 path?

Evan Li: embed-cache + read-through approach sounds right. Router API must be extremely cheap (small JSON) and support a batch lookup endpoint. also consider latency budget: target additional <2ms median for colocated, <10ms remote. needs perf validation.

Maya Thompson: agreed. I'll open a spike to measure: staging endpoints will be: https://staging-router.internal/lookup?tenant={id} and /batch_lookup. I'll add colocated proxy in staging.

Rafael Ortiz: migration runner suggestions: a dry-run that marks tenants as 'migratable' then a phased migration:
```
# mark cohort
./bin/session_migrate --cohort=beta --mark
# execute migration in batches
./bin/session_migrate --cohort=beta --batch=250 --resume
# validate pointers
./bin/session_migrate --cohort=beta --validate
```
Make runner idempotent and record progress to S3 or our job-store for resumption.

Priya Nair: rollback story? if router fails or p99 regresses we need fast flip back. feature flags and routing switch required. also need debug endpoints to force-read-archive (legacy) and to flush router cache.

Maya Thompson: rollback plan short:
1) enable dual-write but keep reads on legacy path for cohort.
2) after backfill and validation, flip reads to router for cohort behind FF.
3) monitor: p50/p99 latency, error-rate, cache-miss rate, fallback count, and compaction errors.
4) on regression -> flip reads back, continue dual-write, investigate.
All flips via ff-service; commands below:
```
# flip reads to router for cohort
curl -X POST https://ff-service.internal/toggle -d '{"feature":"router_read","cohort":"beta","enabled":true}'
# force legacy read
curl https://router.internal/debug?force_legacy=1&tenant={id}
```

Evan Li: observability: add correlation id propagation across router->archive, tag metrics by cohort and migration_id. also instrument cache hit ratio and pointer_version deltas.

Rafael Ortiz: what about transactional semantics for ownership changes during migration? e.g., a tenant ownership flip could occur mid-migrate. CAS on pointer_version is required. prefer single-field CAS API on archive.

Maya Thompson: yes we're standardizing on a CAS write: write(pointer_version, expected_version, new_owner). if expected_version mismatch -> 409 and caller retries. will add client libs to handle exponential backoff.

Priya Nair: cost delta estimation: archive reads will be cheaper per-op but compaction and background read scans add cost. need a rough cost model before wide rollout. Who can estimate RPS * cost delta?

Maya Thompson: @Evan can you run a cost delta calc after the spike? include remote vs colocated NRT numbers.

Evan Li: yes. I'll run perf + cost sim on Wed and post numbers. expect to test both colocated router and remote router.

arch-bot: note: staging/router v0.2 scheduled -> Wed 11:15 UTC (2612223300). CI: unit+integ ok.

Rafael Ortiz: I'll draft the migration runbook and include troubleshooting steps: stale pointer detection, force-resync, and how to disable compaction for impacted tenants. will post tomorrow.

Maya Thompson: action items: Evan -> perf spike Wed, Rafael -> runbook draft Thu, Priya -> cost-model sketch Thu EOD, I'll open RFC PR for router/archive schema and FFs now. any objections? otherwise I'll proceed. :rocket:
